nodes.title: The proof derives the five theorems from one inequality on a weighted prime sum, which it gets by bounding the slope of one lattice from two sides, with m the number of lifts in a chain between unitary groups, which the author's note calls theta lifts, and m near √x
The document follows the route from Main.lean down and names for each step the theorem, what was read and its count

A language model read the route in one session with seven parallel readings and two further comparisons with the Lean text, Gemini, a model of another maker, compared four parts and the list of claims with the Lean text, no mathematician checked it, Lean was not run, and a reading leaves open whether a definition is the object its name suggests
The counts come from compiled files of the build cache, and the README records no complete comparator run on the current source
A constant is a compiled declaration, and a theorem rests on the project declarations its compiled statement and proof reach, Mathlib excluded

nodes.title: Read in full, read at its top and read by statement are three depths of reading, and this session is the model session that wrote the document
Premise, supplied, closed theorem, record and bundle

A datum is a value of the record D7 with a host, lattices, maps, words and the number m of lifts, a family holds a datum for every large x and index, and a host is the record of an auxiliary abelian number field
The slope of a lattice is degree over rank with degree minus log covolume, and mu of a Hermitian lattice is twice the slope with two corrections
The height htMap of a map is the mean over infinite places of the log of the squared operator norm, and the number h of a word is a separate field that bounds it
A link is a condition on a family whose name begins with Link
The note is the author's four-page note, whose timeline has 20 entries
A sentence marked as suggestion, interpretation or guess goes beyond what the Lean text shows
The seven parallel readings and what each read
Step 1. The five theorems follow from zero-freeness of Dirichlet L-functions for real part above 1/2

Step 2. Zero-freeness follows by a Landau argument from an upper bound x^θ, for every θ above 1/2, for the prime sum Gm with its main terms subtracted on intervals from Y to Y^(3/2), for arbitrarily large Y

Step 3. The wanted characters sit among the characters of a host, a subgroup sum removes some unwanted ones, and a count of zeros with a mean square bound shows that at least half of the candidates for q and then for d give the others a prime sum of at most y^(1/2+ε/2) for y from Y to Y^A
Step 4. The sum over all characters of the host equals ASK minus its main term by finite Fourier inversion

Step 5. ASK is bounded through the slope of a lattice, which DIV bounds from above and SlopeIneq from below by a mean over further lattices, while a third condition puts a quantity below the slope of each further lattice and ASK is at most that quantity plus a loss

Step 6. Both bounds concern linear maps into the lattice, one for each word of a datum, and a pairing of each word factors through a chain of m kernels between spaces that carry unitary groups, of ranks k + j(t+1) for j up to m − 1 and k + m(t+1) − 1 on the last space, the first m − 2 composed one after the other, the last two inside a finite sum, with one more linear map after them, and the document does not record how the pairing is tied to the map

Step 7. The main term of the upper bound holds one term a·log a − a − a·logOm per lift and top place, and for one lift interlacing weights and a hook product bound a sum over its weights by a·log a − a plus an error

Step 8. The lower bound applies a general statement about several maps into one lattice, which takes two bounds on products of matrices from a link, proved for a second set of maps and carried to the maps of the words, and one bound on the number of rows, with a family of many words whose existence is a premise not followed, and by the document's interpretation the bounds say that the maps are nearly isometries after scaling in the mean over the family and that the images fill the target evenly
Step 9. The two bounds leave errors of about x/m, m and √x, and m between x^(1/2−ε) and x^(1/2+ε/2), with further premises on the numbers of the error, gives the exponent 1/2 + cε
Which section covers which step, with a short name for each of the nine steps

Further branches supply the premises, namely VWin, Row and a record of 46 fields, five of data and 41 conditions on the families, one of which says that the chains of lifts exist, fed by a covolume bound
The note calls the argument a descendant of Stepanov's, in which multiplicity is hard to find over the integers
Entry 5 of the timeline switches to the sum Σ Λ(n)(X/n − 1) − X log X + (1+γ)X
The Lean definition Gz is the expression of entry 5 and the trivial-character part of Gm

Entries 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 16 and 17 name interlacing weights, iterated theta lifts with m like √X, divisibility, the seesaw, the Bost slope inequality, approximate orthogonality and a weakening of Vandiver
The author writes that Claude provided the timeline and that he has not mastered the surrounding mathematics
A later section names an entry where the Lean text matches it
Statements.lean states five propositions, the first being that a Dirichlet L-function is nonzero for real part above 1/2 except the trivial character at 1
The other four follow through Claim.zeta and Claim.strip, which rest on 9 and 7 declarations and were not read
The calls below everyCharacter run through six theorems that rest on 800,327 down to 54,874 declarations
The first four outline lines are rows 1 to 4, and the fifth builds the record
The passage from three inputs to the statement rests on about 55,000 declarations, and the other 745,000 behind everyCharacter supply the inputs
Green rests on 64 declarations, VWin on 173,628, the record on 463,949 and Row on 195,170
The branches share declarations, because their counts add up to more than 800,327

zero_free_all_of_green_v_win takes Green, VWin and one record and concludes zero-freeness for primitive characters, which imprimitive extends to all characters through finitely many nonzero Euler factors, with the trivial character at s = 1 set aside
Its one-line proof splits into the Landau step, the main inequality, the supply of tied families and the supply of fields
A tied family satisfies ChainTied, ChainTie is a different object, and shape_closed_link_n_of_green is called the shape theorem
Sz x is the sum of Λ(n)(x/n − 1) over n ≤ x and Gz x is Sz x − x log x + (1+γ)x
gChi χ y is the twisted sum plus y times the logarithmic derivative of L(χ,s) at 1, and equals Gz for the trivial character
A level holds a finite set KEPT of primitive characters, and Gm is Gz plus the weighted real parts of gChi over KEPT
formB states that an upper bound Gm x ≤ x^θ on intervals from Y to Y^la for arbitrarily large Y gives no zero with real part above θ for every character of KEPT
The proof uses la = 3/2 and applies the step to every primitive character ψ separately, with the level of the powers of ψ, among whose kept characters ψ lies by Level.mem_cyc
formB reduces to zeroFree_of_rpow_window, and the account has four stages that follow the report except stage 3
Stage 1. The Laplace transform Φ of g(u) = Gm(e^u) continues to real part above 0 with a simple pole of positive-weight residue at every zero, and g grows at most like e^(2u)
Stage 2. On the interval the bound on Gm bounds the Taylor-coefficient integrals at σ+iτ and at σ by a multiple of e^(ηU)/(σ−θ)^k
Stage 3. landau_tails bounds the integral outside the interval by C/σ^k with k = ⌈(1+δ/2)σU⌉
By the session's own calculation the weight peaks at u = k/(σ−2), inside the interval when σ is above 4(1+δ)/δ and U is large
Stage 4. A zero with real part above θ makes a coefficient of size c/d^k with d below σ−θ, which contradicts the bounds for large U
One interval for each Y of an unbounded sequence suffices, because the hypothesis enters once for each large U
By the report the proof uses Mathlib's continuation and nonvanishing on real part at least 1 and no functional equation, and the four lemmas of stage 4 were read by statement
core_gm proves Gm x ≤ x^(1/2 + (eD+eL+7)ε) at one x from a host and two conditions, and since ChebyshevInequalityAtWindowScale asks for eD and eL before ε, the constant c depends on neither ε nor Y
CoreAtH says that a record Data with SizeData₂ and fifteen further conditions exists over the host, and ChainTied is its form for a family

EAtH says that every character of the level induces a character of the host from the set Xp, the characters trivial on A0 with the value 1 at iod, and asks ‖gChi χ x‖ ≤ x^(1/2+ε) for the set Bounded, the characters of Xp that are not kept and all of Xm, where the value at iod is −1, which the document calls the other characters

The field bdG is used by sigA_le alone and filled by supplyOfAdmOf, which takes three premises for the level of the powers of one ψ, from boundedTw, which reads it off PairGood under a condition TwistForm whose source the document does not record

TwistForm says that every character of the host that is trivial on A0 agrees with a power of ψ times the quadratic characters of q and d, each to the exponent 0 or 1, and that its value at iod is 1 or −1 as the exponent of d is 0 or 1

Every character of Bounded has at least one of the two quadratic characters present, since Xm has the exponent 1 of d and a character of Xp that is not kept has the exponent 1 of q, and boundedTw applies PairGood at y = x, where y^(1/2+ε/2) is at most x^(1/2+ε)
WinPair fixes the primes q and d of the host with log q near Y^(ε/5), log d near Y^(ε/5)(log Y)² and divisibility conditions on d + 1

PairGood says that every primitive character inducing a character of modulus M times the quadratic characters of q and d, at least one present, has ‖gChi χ y‖ ≤ y^(1/2+ε/2) for y from Y to an upper end X and a bounded logarithmic derivative, with zero-free boxes for the products with a real character whose modulus divides 8·M, and pairEx proves it with X = Y^A
pairEx proves that such a pair exists for every large Y, through pair_exists and pair_share with η = 1/2
What was read of this section
The field bounds concerns sums whose length is at most a fixed power of the logarithm of the modulus, since Y^A ≤ (2 log q)^(5A/ε)
ThinScales bounds the prime sums far above x, and the code derives its form for a datum from three statements on zeros that litThin proves and whose proofs were not read
pair_share rests on 1,239 declarations and is the source of the square-root bound for the other characters
The two sets of primes, q ≡ 3 mod 8 in a range from z, and d ≡ 7 mod 16 in a range from z′ with q and the small odd primes dividing d + 1
Box asks for a zero-free box of width 1/400, a logarithmic derivative at most C·log Y and ‖Gchi ψ y‖ ≤ y^(1/2+τ) for y from Y to X
GoodQ and GoodD say that Box holds for the primitive characters built from ξ and the Jacobi symbols of q and d, and Gchi equals gChi
pair_share states that all but a share η of the primes q meet GoodQ and for each such q all but a share η of the primes d meet GoodD, and pairEx turns the case η = 1/2 into PairGood
The proof calls stage1 and stage2, both cases of one theorem stage on a set PPset of primes in a residue class between √U and U
stage calls a prime bad when one of at most R twisted characters fails Box, and bounds the bad primes by the share η through two kinds of η/2 each
Bad primes of the first kind, which fail ZeroFreeBox, have share at most a constant times U^(−21/40), from a zero density bound U^(3/8) against at least U^(9/10) primes
Bad primes of the second kind have a truncated sum above y^(1/2+τ)/2, and bad_share gives them a share below η/2 over the R characters
For a prime of neither kind box_of_S proves Box

box_of_S passes from the truncated sum to Gchi, because an identity writes Gchi as minus the truncated sum minus y times a tail, and tailK bounds Y^K times the tail by Y^ε for a character that meets GoodC
The number 400 is the width of the zero-free box and the exponent of the truncation point, and tailK was read by statement
The session guesses that the tail is small because a zero-free box of width 1/400 saves Z^(−1/400) = Y^(−K)
bad_share follows from the mean square premise MeanSq by cutting the interval into dyadic blocks, which gives a share at most (32·C₂/τ)·Y^(−τ)/(1 − 2^(−τ))
meanSqK proves MeanSq by multiplying the square out, with the trivial bound for the pairs where n·n′ is a square and a premise on sums of (p/r) for the others
twistK supplies that premise from the prime number theorem in progressions, a zero-free region, excBound and page_across, with one possible exception

The session's interpretation is that the values (n/p) cancel on average over p as independent signs do, which gives truncated sums of square-root size for most primes, in a range of y far below the modulus
What was read of the pair of primes
Two theorems carry the main inequality, and neither proof contains a theta lift or a lattice, only m copies of one term and real numbers of a record

ch_core assumes the bound of ch_top for ASK − MAIN for every u0 in A0 and twelve conditions, and concludes that GmA, a weighted sum of the real parts of the prime sums of the kept characters, is at most x^(1/2+(C+3)ε) plus SigA, the sum over the characters trivial on A0 and not kept

GPsi is the prime sum of a character, ASK adds 2·log p times the positive parts max(a/p^i − w, 0) over the powers of the inert odd primes up to P with a term for d, MAIN is a·(log a − 1 − γ + L − W) with W the mean of log w over PhiSet, and both depend on t, u0 and the lift j through a and the weights w
Five lemmas carry ch_core, an exact identity ASK − MAIN = De, a common argument, a subgroup sum, the value at x and the division, with a premise on the set TT

Row 1 is finite Fourier inversion because De is a double sum, over the classes outside PhiSet and the characters, of w times GPsi at a/w, row 3 concludes nT·m·b·((nT2/n)/2)·g ≤ Err + 2·nT·m·b/x, and the quantity that row 2 bounds holds no weight w, so the sum over the m lifts multiplies it by m
Row 5 divides the error x^(Cε)·(nT·aE·(1 + m²/k) + m·(B + N)) by nT·m·b times half of nT2/n, under the bounds of RestSize and the premises m ≤ x^(1/2+ε/2) and x·m ≤ k
By the session's arithmetic the division leaves four terms, at most 2x^(1/2+ε), 2, 4x^(1/2+13ε/8) and 2x^(1/2+9ε/8)
The four terms add up to at most 10·x^(1/2+13ε/8), and with the further factors the exponent is 1/2 + (C+3)ε

GrowthSizeBound, which proposition_size_bound proves, has the conclusion of row 3 as premise with G − 4·x^(1/2+ε) in the place of g, its two small terms 4·x^ε/x and 4·x^(1/2+ε) are absorbed by the exponent when 26 ≤ x^(3ε/8), and ch_core applies it to GmA − SigA, which gives the bound for GmA with SigA added

The terms x/m and m are equal at m = √x, the proof takes the window for m as premises and does not choose m, the fourth term is about √x for every m, and core_gm calls ch_core with C = eD + eL + 3, which gives its conclusion one ε more

B0 and Nc are budgets that the code defines by formulas, with B0 = f·m·b·x^ε, so the factor m of the third term is part of the definition of the budget, EComp5 says that the number Ee differs from m times a product of two numbers of the record by at most a constant times m·B0, why the errors of the m lifts fit m times a budget that itself grows with m was not read, and the text takes the premise NumFacts.sw, by which the shift w of lift j is at least s, as showing why the budget has to grow with m
ch_top proves the assumption of ch_core from SizeData₂, a conjunction of eleven conditions on a record Data of 39 numbers and functions

ch_top takes four further premises, of which IdentU sets the fields aT, w, gam, LpL and ASK of the record to the numbers a t, the weights of ASK, γ, the real part of L and the sum of ASK over TT and the lifts, and ErrWindows, LargeX and BNBoundsU are conditions on sizes and budgets
The record has indices u0, u and t, the numbers muCC and Fo depend on u0 and muN, h and T on u0 and u, Main is the sum of MAIN, and ph y is y log y − y
DIV says that muCC + h u − Fo is at most the sum over t of m·(ph(aT t) − aT t·logOm) − aT t·log(T u) plus errors, the one condition where m multiplies the main term

SlopeIneq says, when three numbers of the record lie in stated ranges and HH is positive and at least a difference, that the weighted mean over u of muN u − h u, minus the log of the number of u and corrections, is at most muCC, where HHBound gives HH those two properties and FParams keeps the three numbers below three bounds of the record

QuotientSlopeBoundsWith puts Ga plus Fo below muN u up to further numbers and LossBounds puts ASK below Ga plus a loss, s_lower5 adds DIV, which cancels Fo, and takes the mean with the weights of SlopeIneq, Ga_bound5 adds SlopeIneq, the two bounds for the mean s cancel muCC, and with key_identity5 each_unit_bound_statement concludes ASK ≤ Main plus an explicit error, where the session read the proof of s_lower5 and the reading of six proofs read Ga_bound5 in full
The rest of ch_top fits the errors inside the bound through core_ineq, of which the beginning was read

The record has a positive number w for each lift and each place, and Count5 says that the logarithm of T u is at least the sum over the lifts of the mean over the places of log(w·v/π) plus m·lg minus an error, bounds it from above and bounds its variation over u

Main holds for each lift and each t the product of aT t and log aT t − 1 − gam + LpL − ℓ, with ℓ the mean over the places of log w, logOm is gam + log(π/v) − LpL, and by IdentU gam is γ and LpL the real part of L

key_identity5 shows that with the lower bound of Count5 in place of log T u the main term of DIV equals Main minus m times the sum of aT t times lg plus an error, since the two logarithms of π/v cancel, and EComp5 matches the subtracted term with the number Ee

IdentU ties the w of the record to the weights w of ASK, and TieArith gives those weights as the number e of the lift at the place, which is also the definition of the shift w of the section on one lift
TieLocal says for a family what the numbers of the record measure, with the index u running over the words of the datum of u0
muCC is the slope of the dual of the lattice RR, muN u the slope of the lattice Nu u, h u bounds the height of the map Bk u from Nu u into the dual of RR, and the number of lifts is R.m
The slope inequality is therefore about the maps Bk u of the words of one datum into one lattice, and m enters through the bound h u
For the lattices of a datum the divisibility inequality bounds the dual slope of RR plus h u minus Fo by a main term with m times a sum of ph(aT t)
Seven theorems carry it, from linkDIVt_of_bridge_kernel down to rhs_le_record, and three sums run over a set J of lifts of size m
The first sum is in the height, where each lift contributes at most ph(aT t) at each t, so m lifts give m times that term
The second sum is in the slope, where boundsMu bounds the dual slope of RR by sums over the lifts through five propositions
The third sum is in the chain, where height_chain_atR is submultiplicativity of the operator norm in logarithms

LinkDIV follows from LinkEta and DIVinN, divinN_of_hypV gets DIVinN from a bound HypV for a family and the conditions LinkN and SmallLevelRankEq, by their statements HypV is the bound VVle that supplyOfAdmOf derives from the bound of VWin, how the class of families carries the bound and where the two conditions come from was not read, and LinkDIV at one datum includes BesselId with its two parts
By the form of the bound of VWin this is where entry 17 of the note enters the divisibility, which the text marks as an interpretation
The names match the Bessel period of entry 12
A ColChain holds matrices Kj through whose product the pairing of the datum factors, and a ChainTie identifies them with the kernel operators and the coupling of a KerChain

The group acting on the spaces chF u j is UF E (N j) times two further groups, where UF E r is the isometry group of the form that adds up star (x i) * y i on E^r for a number field E of the datum, and the last space evGSD has the group UF E r of rank N m − 1, which the code extends to the rank N m
UF E r is a unitary group, because the condition conjE says that star is complex conjugation under every embedding of E into the complex numbers
The rank is N j = k + j·(t+1), and entry 8 of the note writes a lift as π ↦ π ⊞ μ_j[t]
That the letter t of the note is this t is an interpretation
Since R.m = m2 + 2, the chain of a word has m2 steps and so m − 1 matrices, with ranks from N 0 to N m because the last matrix covers two lifts
The record ChTh holds m distributions th 0 to th (m−2) and top, equivariant under both unitary groups
The first m − 2 matrices are kernel operators, the last is a coupling built as a finite sum of products of two kernels, and a final linear map follows
Some matrix holds more than one lift, because m lifts sit on m − 1 matrices

rowsU_of_colPins_alt proves for one word of a datum, under conditions on sizes and ties, that the word has a ColChain with a ChainTie, it rests on 14,837 declarations, and by the exact graph its one user is kernel_columns_from_ties_alt, which serves the condition DefiniteSideCondition of the record, while the shape theorem does not reach it
The chain theorem enters the proof through the condition DefiniteSideCondition of the record alone
That the definitions fit a theta kernel for a pair of unitary groups is the session's interpretation from the names

The reading of the chain found the kernels defined from the distributions, the theta-lift conditions ThHyp untraced, the height numbers built in two halves, the supply of adm2 in the proof of the shape theorem, and BesselId in two parts, the isometries from join data of the record and BuRational from buRat_rrFull_closed_alt
A place is a pair of a truth value and an element of H, it carries interlacing numbers u and v and numbers e and b, and the top weight aT t is u 0 − (k−1)/2
The weights nu of lift j come from the numbers uW and from blocks of t + 1 values for each earlier lift

kerPlace is the sum of ph over the weights minus their sum times logOm, logHook is the log of a hook product, hU adds kerPlace and subtracts logHook over places and lifts, and the document does not record how hU is tied to the number h of a word

stepE_num proves under the 32 premises of NumFacts that the sum of ph over the weights minus logHook is at most ph(aT ρ) at a top place and 0 elsewhere up to an error, and that the weights sum to aT ρ + k·w up to a constant times w plus further terms, where w is the number e of the lift at the place
young_diagram_hook says that the sum of the logs of the factorials of the row lengths is at most the log of the hook product
It holds because the hook of a cell is at least as long as the rest of its row, and those lengths multiply to L! along a row of length L

young_diagram_step_origin reaches young_diagram_factorial, which at a place that is not a top place pairs the first k − 1 rows of the lift with the k − 1 rows under the hook product through the interlacing and at a top place pairs only the k − 2 middle rows, where the top row has the length aT + w − s, and the j rows from the numbers b take no part
Each lift contributes at most ph(aT t) plus an error at a top place, and kerPlace multiplies the weight sum aT t + k·w by logOm, while the main term of DIV holds m·(ph(aT t) − aT t·logOm)

By a comparison run of 24 November the terms that are linear in w and hold logOm cancel inside divisor_inequality_assembly up to a multiple of the absolute value of w, and the logarithm of w enters Main through the number T u
The document does not record where the proof puts the terms that contain s
numFacts_rec proves the premises of stepE_num for a family from size conditions

Four guesses from names and the note, logOm as the Chowla-Selberg period, the hook product as the Weyl dimension formula, the interlacing as that of entry 7 and the number of lifts as the multiplicity

Frame_at says that the weighted mean s of mu − h over the words, minus the logarithm of the number of words and a correction built from the excess, η, e and HH, is at most the dual slope of RR, and the proofs of frame_at_of and joint_a_ramified_holds were read in full

JointARam is a statement without a datum about a family of lattices with maps into one target lattice, whose premises are the geometry LatGeom, the numbers LatNum, a factorisation of each matrix into a first factor and an isometry with a lost share of columns, three bounds InputSG on the first factors and sizes bounded by σ ≤ 1/20, and whose conclusion is the inequality of Frame_at with 2·e0 for e and 5σ plus three times the square root of the lost share for η

The proof has two parts, ramification_linear_case_holds, which turns the three bounds into a bound on the trace of Q² and a bound on the distances of the Gram matrices from the identity, and the frame theorem of the folder HarderNarasimhan, whose proof through frame_theorem_sharp is unread

frame_at_of applies the general statement with the words as members, the lattices Nu u, the maps Bk u, the dual of RR as target and σ = x^(−CH), takes the matrices and the three bounds from FrameReal_at, and for a family the factor η + 4·√e of the correction is at most 6σ, since FrameRealF asks 3·√(lost share) + 4·√eB ≤ σ and frameF_of takes 5σ + 3·√(lost share) as the bound for η
The words together have at least Dstar/σ columns, because each has at least Dstar/(C0·Γ²) by ChProviso_at and there are at least C0·Γ²·x^CH of them by ChCode_at
The two conditions are parts of the condition Chosen on a family, DesignExists says that families with Chosen exist, and where DesignExists is proved was not read

Each word has a space of dimension duS u with a map Pu u into one Hilbert space, the block KD u u′ is the scaled product of the adjoint of Pu u with Pu u′, hsSq is its squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm and hsDiagFull that of KD u u minus the identity

LinkS_at is an implication from ChProviso_at to three bounds, hsSq u u′ ≤ (1+η0)·duS u·duS u′/Dstar, hsDiagFull u ≤ e0·duS u and Dall ≤ (1+η1)·Dstar, and the link gives η0, η1 and √e0 at most exp(−x^(ε/8)), which is below σ/2 for large x

The maps Pu u and the maps Bk u are different maps, BlockReal_at says that the matrix of Bk u is the block on the rows of the target of the matrix of Pu u, up to a conjugation, times an isometry, blockReal_at_of proves it from BesselId, matK_at_of states the first two bounds for the first factors of the maps Bk u, Dall stands where the general statement has the number of rows when the target has Drows rows, and what Dstar and Dall are was not opened

The session's interpretation is that the second bound makes the first factor of each word an isometry up to a small relative error in the mean over its columns, and the maps themselves only in the sum over the family, that the first factors have at least 19 times and the maps at least 14 times as many columns as there are rows so the images overlap as random subspaces do, that the trace condition makes the images fill the target evenly, and that the logarithm of the number of words is the price of the mean
linkCore builds every witness of ChainTied from a family, with none left free, and the reading names no source for HidaSetting
The source of each part of SizeData₂, as the reading reports it
topDesWin takes the links as premises and concludes FamilyClassConnected, which the premise of zeroFreeAll_of_topG asks for, and seven theorems supply the links in the proof of the shape theorem
Green goes to the supplier of LinkIRR alone and is derived from a statement on regular characters that the project proves

The shape theorem takes Green and concludes TopShapeAlt, which has 53 binders of data and hypotheses, and goal_of_shape_of_hyps fills 51 of them, 45 from one field each of the record of 46 fields and six from the remaining field, a selection σ
The other two hypotheses, hVC and nR, are the proposition True in this use and are filled with trivial

VWin says that the lengths shaLen of certain Galois cohomology groups are finite and that the sum of log l times the lengths is at most √exp(x^ε), for subfields of cyclotomic fields cut out by ψ, q, d and an exponent
The formula suggests the group of entry 17 of the note, with an added condition at the places above l
The bound is used to declare a host good and to absorb a term of the divisibility inequality
For each fixed B the allowed bound exp(x^ε/2) exceeds x^B once x is large

The proof runs through five theorems read at their tops, down to ferreroWashington and bounds on lengths in five cases, with statements named after Poitou-Tate, Greenberg-Wiles and Bloch-Kato filled by project theorems
Row says that every regular algebraic polarized cuspidal representation of GL_n over a CM field has a continuous semisimple Galois representation with the condition PropsB
Its proof combines a theta lift existence theorem with a geometric realisation, and of 77 Published statements behind it 69 have a closed proving theorem and 8 only derivations
Row is passed on to VWin and into the record OpenLiteratureStatements
